syntax.rationale: The page's declaration surface is split across the 'shape of the feature' subsections. #scroll-state-query (Step 2) carries the @container scroll-state() query call form; the feature/value grammar is #features (mapped to inputs) and the container-establishment declaration (container-type: scroll-state) is the preceding Step 1.

errors.rationale: CSS scroll-state() is declarative with no throwing surface: invalid or unsupported feature/value pairs are dropped by the general CSS error-recovery rules, which the page does not single out, so there is no page-documented error path to map.

securityPrivacy.rationale: scroll-state() is a rendering-only CSS feature: #why explains it replaces JavaScript observer polling with a synchronous paint-pass style, exposing no new script or data surface, and the page documents no security or privacy consideration.

notes: B3 unit (gendn-g8o): the page carried zero id attributes, so six existing headings gained ids (at-a-glance, why, syntax, features, example, browser-support) and nothing else in the page changed. The syntax dimension anchors #syntax (Step 1: establish a scroll-state container), which carries the container-type: scroll-state / container-name declaration in a <pre><code> block; the page's declaration surface is otherwise split across the adjacent 'shape of the feature' subsections — 'Step 2: query with @container scroll-state()' (the query call form) and 'Supported scroll-state features' (#features, the feature/value grammar) — so no single fragment contains the whole surface. CARRIED DIVERGENCES, BOTH SIDES, NEITHER ADJUDICATED: (1) the page's 'Supported scroll-state features' table lists 'both' as a scrollable value, but the live spec's scrollable value list is 'none | top | right | bottom | left | block-start | inline-start | block-end | inline-end | x | y | block | inline' with no 'both' (the spec lists 'both' only for the snapped feature). (2) the page documents three scroll-state features (stuck, snapped, scrollable) — matching the live ChromeStatus summary — but the cited live spec (drafts.csswg.org/css-conditional-5/#scroll-state) additionally defines a fourth feature 'scrolled' (none | top | right | bottom | left | block-start | inline-start | block-end | inline-end | x | y | block | inline) that the page does not mention. (3) the page's 'at a glance' and 'browser support' state the feature shipped in Chrome 149 (desktop + Android), but the live ChromeStatus record 5072263730167808 reports milestone 133 (desktop 133, android 133, webview 133, status 'Enabled by default', last updated 2025-08-25).
